Visited Ramashraya multiple times over the years, and every visit for everyone only strengthens the admiration for this legendary place. The food here is consistently outstanding — honestly, the taste is better than most South Indian restaurants even in the South itself!

Every dish is served fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced in taste and texture. From the idlis and dosas to the upma and filter coffee, everything is up to the mark. The service is quick, the staff are polite, and the overall atmosphere reflects the charm of old-school Mumbai hospitality.

Despite being busy almost all day, the place maintains excellent hygiene and efficiency. It’s one of those rare eateries that has truly stood the test of time — since 1939 — and continues to deliver authentic South Indian flavors with unmatched consistency.

A must-visit landmark for anyone who appreciates quality, tradition, and genuine taste.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

featured_reviews.name: BhataktiAatmaWasHere
featured_reviews.review_text:
A school friend sent me a reel about Poe and Pao in Chembur. I decided to go chasing Poe and Pao. Since I was already in Bandra, I thought I’d try their Matunga outlet instead.

Now, if you’re a true-blue Mumbaikar, you know traffic jams aren’t an inconvenience, they’re a lifestyle. So there I was, stuck in the middle of one, wishing for a restroom more than anything else.

When I finally reached, they said, “Go next door.” I stumbled into Dakshin Culture Curry and found the cleanest restroom in Mumbai. Small, but spotless. You can’t do pranayama there, but you’ll definitely come out feeling zen.

Feeling human again, I stepped out… and somehow found myself in Diva Maharashtracha. For a moment, I thought I’d taken a wrong turn in life. That’s when someone explained that Dakshin Culture Curry, Goa Portuguesa, and Diva Maharashtracha are a trilogy, same team, shared menu, different cuisines. And Poe and Pao? The latest addition to the family.

One look at the menu, and I knew there was no way I was walking back to Poe and Pao.

I started with a Sushegad Shot (feni, lime, and kaffir leaves) -  Goa in a glass. Then came the Khekade Kalimiri Soup, a crab-and-black-pepper combo that doubles as a natural sinus reliever. After that, Ravas Moile, Tender Coconut Cashew Nut Sukke (their signature dish), Chicken Modak, and Appam n Amboli.

The Chicken Modak was the surprise star—moist chicken kheema wrapped in a soft, pillowy coating. Though, between us, it did look slightly jaundiced.

They ended the meal with complimentary Caramel Custard—light, soft, and just the right sweetness.

The staff were courteous and attentive, the ambience warm and welcoming.

Ambience: A+
Food: A+++

What started as a quest for Poe and Pao turned into a delicious detour, a reminder that some of the best finds in Mumbai happen purely by serendipity.

What truly made this place special was the personal touch. The owner personally visited every table, warmly sharing the inspiring journey of how the restaurant began. He spoke about his wife’s culinary journey and her exceptional talent as a cook—the heart behind the delicious recipes served here. Listening to their story made the food taste even better, knowing it comes from passion, dedication, and love.

The restaurant has grown into multiple branches, including international locations, and it’s easy to see why. This place is not just about food—it’s about culture, stories, and genuine hospitality.

✨ Highly recommended for anyone who loves authentic Goan cuisine, soulful music, and heartfelt hospitality. A place you’ll want to visit again and again.

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Udupi Shri Krishna Restaurant, which is conveniently located just a 1-minute walk from Matunga East Railway Station—making it extremely easy to reach without any hassle.

I learned that the restaurant was inaugurated by Sane Guruji, which adds a nice historical and cultural touch to the place.

When we arrived, we had to wait in the coupon queue, but it was quite smooth. Within about 10 minutes, our name was called. Considering it was a Saturday, the waiting time was very reasonable. I’ve heard that sometimes the wait can go up to 45 minutes to an hour, but we were lucky.

The staff at the counter was very polite and attentive. One thing that stood out was how they reminded everyone to wash their hands before eating—such a small yet thoughtful and caring gesture.

The food is served on a banana leaf, which adds a traditional and authentic feel. The entire meal felt fresh, simple, and very much like home-cooked food.

The thali included:

2 sabjis
1 koshimbir (cucumber salad)
Roti and puri
Curd
Pickle
Buttermilk
Nimbu rasam and regular rasam
Rice with ghee
One sweet (options like rasgulla, halwa, shrikhand, or gulab jamun)

Curd and sweets are limited, while the rest is unlimited.

The taste was excellent—especially the curd and nimbu rasam, which were absolutely delicious. The rasgulla we had was fresh, mildly sweet, and exceeded expectations.

The management and service were top-notch. The staff ensured that hot food was served in every round, which made the experience even better. Overall, it truly felt like having a comforting meal at home.

The full thali costs ₹300, and the mini thali is ₹200, which is quite reasonable for the quality and quantity offered.

My only suggestion would be to introduce a premium thali option at a slightly higher price, including a few more South Indian dishes for those who want to explore more variety.

Overall, a wonderful experience—highly recommended to everyone! 👍

featured_reviews.name: DV
featured_reviews.review_text: This is an iconic eatery that is as old as 84 years. It's is a true treasure for Mumbaikars who like South Indian vegetarian food. It serves a full unlimited meal from the south Indian cuisines with Tamil dishes being prominently cooked and served. It's traditionally served on a banana leaf making it visually appealing. The Thali as it is known has Rasam, Sambar, Dal, Rice with option of ghee atop, Poori, Chapati, 2 dry cooked vegetables and 2 gravy based vegetables. There is curd and flavoured (ginger/coriander) butter milk. There is a choice of dessert; my favourite is the Moong Dal payasam. At a modest 300/- bucks it's absolutely value for money. It's a living testament of cultural bonding between the South Indian community and the local Maharashtrians as well as Gujratis. The fact that it was inaugurated by Sane Guruji makes it even richer in identity.

Known for its crispy dosas, soft idlis, and rich, aromatic filter coffee, every bite feels comforting and nostalgic. The ambiance is simple yet inviting, perfect for casual catch-ups or a relaxed solo meal. Service is quick, and the food quality is consistently impressive. Whether you’re craving a hearty breakfast or a light evening snack, this café delivers on both taste and experience. A must-visit for anyone who loves traditional South Indian food in Mumbai with a homely touch and great value.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Fulsundar
featured_reviews.review_text:

We tried the strawberry milkshake & mango milkshake both were thick, chilled, and refreshing. The paper masala dosa was big, crispy, and came with good chutney and sambar. Kanchipuram idli was soft and flavourful, a little different from regular idli and worth trying.
Cheese tava rice was spicy, cheesy, and filling good if you’re very hungry. We ended with pineapple sheera, which was warm, slightly sweet, and had a nice fruity taste.
Overall, it’s a good place for South Indian food and quick snacks near the station.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re in Dadar and craving authentic South Indian flavors any time of the day, Muttuswami Cafe is the place to be!
This is the only café in the area open 24/7, making it a perfect spot for early breakfasts, late-night cravings, or casual meetups at any hour.
The food quality is outstanding, with every dish served fresh, flavorful, and satisfying:
Cheese Pav Bhaji – perfectly buttery with a generous layer of melted cheese that elevates the classic taste.
Podi Idli – soft, bite-sized idlis coated beautifully in spicy podi masala and ghee.
Muttuswami Special Benne Dosa – rich, crispy, and soaked in butter with a delicious traditional touch.
Spring Dosa – a unique fusion twist, crispy outside with a flavorful stuffed filling inside.
Fruit Custard Dessert – creamy, refreshing, and loaded with fresh fruits for the perfect sweet ending.
Their fresh juices are equally impressive — especially the pomegranate juice and the orange-mosambi mix, both refreshing and naturally sweet.
What truly makes the experience special is the warm and polite staff. The service is quick, attentive, and always delivered with a smile. The beautiful interiors create a clean, cozy, and welcoming atmosphere, making you want to sit back and enjoy your meal.

Ayyapan Idli Stall, BKC is a simple, casual, and affordable South Indian restaurant serving authentic vegetarian and Jain food. The focus here is on traditional flavours rather than fancy presentation, and the food speaks for itself. They have self service and each dish is served with coconut chutney, tomato chutney and sambar.

Recommended items:

1. Podi Dosa – A simple yet outstanding dosa coated with aromatic podi and ghee, giving it authentic flavour.

2. Benne Podi Dosa – Soft on the inside, crispy on the outside, and generously layered with white butter and podi, making it rich and satisfying.

3. Thatte Idli – Large, pillowy-soft idli with a light texture that practically melts in your mouth.

4. Medu Vada – Perfectly crunchy on the outside and soft, fluffy, and airy on the inside.

5. Filter Coffee – Strong, aromatic, and authentic South Indian filter coffee with a rich coffee flavour.

A great place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian food without spending too much.

You should definitely visit Ayyappan Idli once atleast.

Appam with coconut stew is amazing as well. Especially the stew was so delicious. Mysore onion dosa feels rich in flavour and is prepared in pure ghee. Kanchipuram idli was a decent one and a bit sour. Paniyaram was a one-of-a-kind and is a must try. Cheese pav bhaji was not bad but failed to meet the bar raised by other food items. For desserts, you have to have the pineapple sheera and you can thank me later. A south indian cuisines is incomplete with the iconic filter coffee and the coffee here will not disappoint you. The service is super quick and they serve you unlimited Sambar and Chutney

This restaurant was hitting home-runs after home-runs and I was about to give this place the coveted 5-star rating when they committed a hygienic blunder. I found a small hair in their Pav. If you're in Mahim and craving authentic South Indian breakfast, look no further than this charming dosa joint serving up traditional benne-style dosas that will transport you straight to the heart of Karnataka. The dosas here are perfectly crisp on the outside, yet soft and buttery on the inside, cooked with generous ghee that adds a rich depth of flavor. The taste is simply unparalleled and truly authentic.

What stands out even more is the impressive variety of South Indian breakfast options they offer. From idlis to vadas, upmas, sheera etc, they serve a delightful mix of dishes that are perfect for any craving. But one dish you absolutely cannot miss is their Masala Aloo Bhaji which is the filling inside the dosas. Unlike many places, their masala aloo bhaji is oil-free. Instead of oil, they use water to cook the potatoes, resulting in a flavourful, yet lighter version of this classic dish. It's surprising how much taste they've packed in with this unique preparation—it’s hearty, spicy, and utterly delicious without feeling greasy.

The restaurant’s commitment to authentic flavours, healthy cooking methods, and quality ingredients truly make it a standout in the Mahim area for anyone looking for a satisfying and flavourful South Indian breakfast.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mani’s Lunch Home-
Since 2007, during my monthly early morning office tours, I make it a personal ritual to stop at Mani’s Lunch Home in Matunga East for breakfast. No matter how early the day begins or how packed the schedule looks, I always get down here first—it’s my way of starting the day on the right note.
Over the years, I’ve tasted nearly every item served here. But my usual favorites are the idli-vada, medu vada, and the classic sada dosa. The idlis are soft and fluffy, the vadas crispy and golden, and the dosa—light, thin, and perfectly roasted. Each dish is accompanied by hot sambar and fresh coconut chutney that bring out authentic South Indian flavors.
One of the best parts of Mani’s is their warm and generous service. The staff pours unlimited sambar and chutney on your plate until you gently say “enough.” This simple yet heartfelt gesture has become the USP (Unique Selling Point) of the place. It's not just about the food, but the love and hospitality that comes with it.
Once I finish my meal, I always end with a cup of their aromatic filter coffee. Whether you prefer it light or strong, Mani’s coffee is brewed to perfection—rich, bold, and served in traditional steel tumblers that enhance its charm. For health-conscious guests like me, they also offer sugar-free tea, which is light, refreshing, and perfect to start the workday with clarity and balance.
After breakfast, I continue with my day feeling satisfied and refreshed. That peaceful moment at Mani’s sets a positive tone for whatever work lies ahead.
Mani’s Lunch Home is not just a restaurant for me. It’s a monthly ritual, a memory lane of flavors, and a place where time slows down—where every bite takes me back to the roots of comfort and tradition. In a fast-moving city like Mumbai, Mani’s is a calm, soulful corner that never changes.

featured_reviews.name: Ram Subramanian (Ram)
featured_reviews.review_text: Manis lunch home has always been my favorite spot from my college days in Matunga.On a Sunday I had some work in Matunga so decided to visit Manis lunch home . I ordered Idli vada sambar while my wife ordered lemon rice.The idli vada sambar was very good compared to all the ones I tasted in & around Mumbai. It was very close to the taste in southern part of India. In my college days visit to this restaurant made me nostalgic.As usual even after 24 years they still maintain the restaurant neat & clean. They still serve unlimited sambar & chutney with the dishes.I loved their chutney more than their sambar.The taste of idli vada was same as that tasted four year/ even 24 years before.It was always difficult to get a place to sit inside the restaurant during weekends especially the peak hours. Today we went at an odd time of 11 am so we could comfortably sit inside the small restaurant.The lemon rice was served with kerala pappadam & chutney. It tasted good. The rice looked bulky similar to that used in Kerala.Overall it tasted good.Then although my stomach was full I wanted to taste their plain dosa to which I am a bigger fan.The dosa taste amazing good & kudos to the team for maintaining their standards over the years. Visited Cafe Mysore, Matunga with high expectations as it’s one of the well-known South Indian spots in Mumbai. Unfortunately, the experience didn’t quite live up to the hype.
We tried the Gadbad Idli, which sounded interesting on the menu, but taste-wise it was quite average and not up to the mark. The flavors felt unbalanced and it lacked the authentic punch you expect from a classic Matunga eatery.
We also ordered the Dilkhush Dosa (stuffed). The presentation was decent, but again, the taste didn’t justify the reputation or the pricing. It felt heavy and not particularly flavorful.
What disappointed us more was the customer service. The staff seemed disinterested and inattentive, which affected the overall dining experience. When a place carries such a strong reputation, basic hospitality should match the food quality.

Would consider revisiting only if there’s noticeable improvement.

featured_reviews.name: DNB Travel & Food Reviews
featured_reviews.review_text:
Classic South Indian Favourite with Great Food but Limited Parking

Review:
Cafe Mysore is one of Matunga’s iconic South Indian eateries — an institution famed for its authentic idlis, dosas, rasam vada, and filter coffee that have been delighting locals and food lovers for generations. The food is fresh, hearty, and very reasonably priced, making it a go-to breakfast or lunch spot for both regulars and first-timers. The dosa varieties (especially Dilkhush, Mysore masala) and pineapple sheera are often recommended by customers.

The ambience is casual and simple — not fancy, but clean and welcoming. It’s often busy during peak times (especially weekends and mornings), so be prepared for a bit of a crowd and sharing tables, which contributes to its classic local charm.

What We Loved 👍
Authentic South Indian flavours with generous portions.

Quick service most of the time for breakfast and tiffin items.

Pocket-friendly pricing.

Good for family breakfasts and casual meets.

Seating and comfort are basic; the place fills up quickly during rush hours.

Parking & Access 🚗
There is no dedicated parking lot or valet service at the cafe itself.

Being right on Matunga’s King’s Circle area, finding street parking can be challenging, especially during peak morning and evening hours. You may need to park in nearby public parking areas or use paid parking zones near the circle and walk a short distance.

If driving isn’t convenient, the cafe is very well connected by local transport, with King’s Circle railway station just a short walk away.

Best For: Authentic South Indian breakfast/lunch, quick meals, family outings, casual meet-ups.

The Peri Peri Fried Idli was perfectly crunchy with amazing flavor.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had an amazing experience at this South Indian restaurant! The food was absolutely authentic and full of flavor. The dosas were perfectly crisp on the outside and soft inside, and the sambar had that rich, homemade taste with just the right balance of spices. Overall, great value for money and a must-visit if you love South Indian food. I’ll definitely be coming back!
